ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Choosing definitive evaluation

A stable toddler has a convincing aspiration history, unilateral decreased air entry, and air trapping on chest radiography. The pediatric airway team considers further assessment. Which procedure can both visualize the airway and permit object removal?

  1. Bronchoscopy
  2. Low-dose chest CT
  3. Inspiratory and expiratory radiographs
  4. Flexible nasolaryngoscopy limited to the upper airway
  5. Esophagoscopy
Answer and explanation

Bronchoscopy

Bronchoscopy directly evaluates the tracheobronchial tree and can allow retrieval by an experienced team.

Option explanations

Bronchoscopy: Bronchoscopy directly evaluates the tracheobronchial tree and can allow retrieval by an experienced team.

Low-dose chest CT: CT can help selected uncertain cases but cannot itself retrieve an object.

Inspiratory and expiratory radiographs: These can demonstrate air trapping but do not directly remove the obstruction.

Flexible nasolaryngoscopy limited to the upper airway: This examines proximal structures but does not provide definitive evaluation and removal of a bronchial object.

Esophagoscopy: This assesses the esophagus rather than the suspected tracheobronchial location.
